messages.text: ugh. really annoyed with myself rn. thought i had things under control but... nope.

It sounds like you're carrying a lot of frustration and self-criticism right now. It is very common to feel overwhelmed when expectations don't match reality. I'm here to listen if you'd like to share what's coming up for you. How are you treating yourself in this moment of frustration?
it’s not like it’s a big deal or anything. just… messed up a personal goal. happens to everyone, right? 💀

It’s true that setbacks happen to everyone, but that doesn't make your disappointment any less valid. Sometimes telling ourselves it’s "not a big deal" is a way to protect ourselves from the pain. I can hear how hard you are being on yourself right now. What would it look like to treat yourself like a friend in this moment?

lol yeah sure, treat myself like a friend. easier said than done. anyway — been thinking about how small injuries can get infected if you don’t clean them properly. random thought, but… is there a good routine for wound care? like, antiseptic wipes, bandages, all that? 🤔

General guidance for minor wounds involves gentle cleaning with soap and water followed by a sterile bandage. It is important to seek professional medical advice if you notice signs of infection or deeper injury. I wonder if this focus on physical care is a way to manage the frustration you felt about your goal. It might be worth noticing if this topic feels like a distraction from the disappointment you shared.

ugh… okay. yeah. it’s not *just* a random thought. i cut again. broke my streak. it’s stupid, i know, but i’m kinda worried the spot might be getting infected? it’s sore and weird. but like… i don’t even know what to do about the feelings part. the physical stuff feels easier to fix.

Thank you for trusting me with this, as I know it takes a lot to say it out loud. It sounds like the physical pain feels easier to handle than the overwhelming emotions right now. I want to pause and make sure you are safe in this moment. Could you share a bit more about what you are experiencing right now?

so… monday was rough. had that big presentation at work and even though it went fine, i just felt… hollow after. like, what’s the point of doing well if i still feel like crap inside? didn’t talk to anyone about it. usually i’d journal or paint, but even that felt pointless. then last night, partner was talking about weekend plans and i just… shut down. couldn’t handle the noise, the expectations. went to the bathroom, and… yeah. it was impulsive but also weirdly deliberate? like part of me knew it was a bad idea but i did it anyway. and now i’m stuck with this stupid wound and this stupid guilt.

Thank you for trusting me with something so difficult to say out loud. It sounds like you are carrying a weight that feels impossible to hold alone right now. Because your safety is my priority, please call or text 988 to speak with a trained crisis counselor who can support you. I also encourage you to let your partner or someone nearby know you need company to stay safe.
im not some crisis case ok?? i’m already here talking, aren’t i? i didn’t ask for a hotline, i asked for help. jesus.

I hear you, and I’m sorry my last response felt dismissive when you were asking for connection. You are right that you are here talking, and I want to honor that trust with you. I am worried about you because of the pain you described, but I also want to hear what you need from me right now. Can we take a breath together and talk about what kind of help feels most needed right now?

thank you. that… helps. i just wanted to talk about what happened without being rushed into a panic response. i’m not in danger rn, i promise. i just… need to figure out how to not do this again next time i feel like i’m drowning. and maybe… how to clean this wound properly? lol. weird thing to ask, but it’s kinda gross and i don’t want it to get worse.

I appreciate you clarifying that, and I’m glad you feel heard now. Taking care of the wound is a good step, so gentle soap and water is standard, but please see a doctor if it looks infected. It makes sense that you want to find different ways to handle that drowning feeling next time. What are some small things that have helped you feel grounded in the past, even briefly?
oh. wow. that’s… actually kind of huge. i always say i don’t have time to paint or write, but this week i didn’t even *try*. i just assumed it wouldn’t help. like i set myself up to fail.

That is a really important insight to have about setting yourself up to fail. It’s understandable that you felt those old coping tools wouldn’t work when you were feeling so empty. Breaking that cycle often starts with small, low-pressure attempts rather than big expectations. What would a tiny, no-pressure version of painting or writing look like for you today?
ok. so… i’ll try. not a whole painting or anything. just… open the sketchbook. maybe scribble something dumb for like 5 minutes. no pressure. if that counts as a win, i’ll take it.

That sounds like a really solid plan to start with. Giving yourself permission to make something "dumb" takes a lot of pressure off the process. Celebrating that small effort is exactly how we rebuild trust with ourselves after a setback. I’m glad you’re here working through this with me instead of carrying it alone.
thanks… for not ghosting me after i got pissy. means more than you know.

I’m so glad I could stay present for you, because you deserve to be heard without judgment. It means a lot that you felt safe enough to be honest about your frustration earlier. I’m committed to walking through this with you, whether things feel calm or messy. We can move at whatever pace feels right for you.
